text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Tuesday.

LONDON - The UK's leading share index snapped out of a six-day losing streak as bid speculation, coupled with a solid rebound on Wall Street, lifted sentiment, dealers said. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,596.3, up 20.5 points, or 0.45 percent.

FRANKFURT - Stocks took their lead from a rebound on Wall Street in late afternoon European trade to post modest gains. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,755.82, up 1.10 points, or 0.03 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,761.07, up 12.28 points, or 0.33 percent.

PARIS - Stocks ended an extremely active session higher, bolstered by a turnaround on Wall Street and firmer European bond prices. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,784.76, up 22.56 points, or 0.82 percent.

ZURICH - Shares ended slightly lower in volatile trade, ending a four-day record run after the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) set an all-time intraday high of 5,611 points, the first time it has broken above 5,600. The Swiss market index closed at 5,576.1, down 11.7 points, or 0.21 percent.

MILAN - The stock market finally took a break from its recent bull run after setting fresh index peaks and ended unchanged after choppy trading. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,316, down 1 point, or 0.01 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares recovered to end with slim gains as markets decided not to take the threat of a Japanese sale of U.S. Treasury bonds too seriously. The AEX index closed at 861.06, up 0.20 points, or 0.02 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks ended with losses, hurt by Wall Street's plunge on Monday following remarks made by Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about U.S. Treasuries. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,341.93, down 94.21 points, or 0.46 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed lower in volatile trading as investors took the weak U.S. market as an excuse to trim their holdings ahead of the long weekend, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 14,890.96, down 130.27 points, or 0.87 percent.

SYDNEY - The share market closed weaker but off its lows as investors factored in a potential Wall Street recovery later after the Dow pulled back 192 points on Monday. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,688.4, down 17.9 points, or 0.66 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Industrial shares ended firm in active trade after recovering from an early slide spurred by Wall Street's slip on Monday night, dealers said. The All-share index closed at 7,333.6, up 47.3 points, or 0.65 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1,018.6, up 3.5 points, or 0.65 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,624.2, up 55.4 points, or 0.34 percent.
